title: Unknown USB drive found in the car park
symptom: An employee found a USB stick in the car park and wants to find its owner
user_description: I found this USB stick in the car park. I'll plug it into my PC and see whose it is so I can give it back.

options.text: Plug it into a spare PC to find the owner
options.why: Even a spare PC can be infected and may be connected to the network. Unknown drives can run harmful software the moment they connect.

options.text: Open the files on your own personal laptop
options.why: Puts a personal device and its data at risk. Unknown drives are never safe to open.

options.text: Tell him not to plug it in, hand it to IT or security, and note where and when it was found
options.why: Attackers leave USB drives on purpose, hoping someone plugs them in. Handing it over lets security examine it safely.
Removes the risk from him, but security loses the chance to learn whether the company is being targeted.

hints: Why might someone leave a USB stick where staff will find it?
What can a USB drive do just by being plugged in?
real_world_tip: Thank the user for asking first. People who check before plugging in are exactly the habit you want to encourage.
